newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli businessmen seek meeting with Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israeli businessmen seek meeting with Arafat.

text.p: A group of leading Israeli businessmen sought Thursday to arrange a meeting with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to discuss ways to advance economic ties.

Benjamin Gaon, president and chief executive of Koor Industries, Israel's largest holding concern, telephoned Arafat's office to urge him to arrange the meeting in the next two weeks. A spokesman was unable to provide details.

Economic benefits have been slim since Israel and the Palestinians signed a peace accord in 1993. Last week's bout of Israeli-Palestinian violence in the West Bank, the Gaza Strip and East Jerusalem shattered the confidence of many investors.

The Israeli businessmen were to have met Arafat in Gaza two weeks ago, but the meeting was cancelled at the last minute due to the arrival of U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross. No new date had been set.
Gaon has been an outspoken advocate of Middle East peace, which has brought Israel economic rewards, including the opening of new markets for trade and higher foreign investment.

The Palestinian Ministry of Economy and Trade said Wednesday that Palestinian losses had risen from $6 million daily before last week's violence to about $10 million because of the crippling Israeli travel restrictions imposed on Palestinian territory after the recent clashes, in which 73 people were killed.
Even before the latest violence, Israel maintained a closure on the West Bank and Gaza that restricted foreign trade and limited work permits for Palestinians seeking jobs in Israel.
